subject: general
question: A shopkeeper buys 20 pens at ₹15 each and another 30 pens at ₹10 each. He mixes all the pens and sells them at ₹14 each. What is the profit or loss per pen he makes on an average?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total pens = 20 + 30 = 50 pens.

Weighted Average CP = (20 × 15 + 30 × 10) ÷ 50.

Average CP = (300 + 300) ÷ 50 = 600 ÷ 50 = ₹12 per pen.

Selling Price (SP) = ₹14 per pen.

Profit per pen = SP − CP = 14 − 12 = ₹2.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2 profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Quantity 1** = 20, **Rate 1** = ₹15; **Quantity 2** = 30, **Rate 2** = ₹10; **SP** = ₹14.
Formulas: Total CP = (Q₁ × C₁) + (Q₂ × C₂) | Average CP = Total CP ÷ Total Quantity | Profit = SP − CP
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d50df1d70232f0949aaa3dd56b031829802b7cc31427045888b5930033b7ffb.png] 
⇒ Total CP = (20 × 15) + (30 × 10) = 300 + 300 = ₹600.
⇒ Total Quantity = 20 + 30 = 50 pens.
⇒ Average CP per pen = 600 ÷ 50 = ₹12.
⇒ Selling Price per pen = ₹14.
⇒ Profit per pen = 14 − 12 = ₹2.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2 profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Cost

When items of different prices are mixed, the average cost price is calculated by dividing the total cost of all items by the total quantity.

Profit and Loss

If Selling Price (SP) > Cost Price (CP), it is a Profit. Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
